en.name: Homemade vinaigrette
en.summary: A homemade vinaigrette is oil, vinegar or citrus, and whatever you have put in it — mustard, shallot, garlic, herbs. It belongs in the fridge and keeps about 2–3 weeks. Freezing does not work, because the emulsion splits.
en.pantry: The counter is the wrong place for a homemade vinaigrette. The acid helps, but raw garlic, shallot or fresh herbs suspended in oil are low-acid produce in an oxygen-poor environment, and that combination belongs cold rather than on a shelf. Bring the jar out for the meal, then put it back — two hours at room temperature is the rule, one hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Keep it sealed at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where it runs about 2–3 weeks. Make it in a clean jar each time rather than topping up an old one, and label it with the date. Olive oil goes cloudy and semi-solid in the cold, which alarms people unnecessarily: stand the jar out for a few minutes while you dress the leaves and shake it hard, and it pours again. A vinaigrette with fresh garlic or shallot in it is best made in smaller quantities and used at the earlier end of the range.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for homemade vinaigrette, and freezing it defeats the purpose. The emulsion splits on thawing into oil above a watery, sedimented layer, and no amount of shaking properly reunites them. A vinaigrette takes two minutes to make from ingredients you already have, so make what you need. Leftovers are better used as a marinade or spooned over roasted vegetables.
spoilage: A rancid, crayon-like smell from the oil
Bubbles, fizzing or cloudiness, particularly in a dressing containing garlic
Mould around the rim or on the surface
Fresh herbs gone slimy and dark in the jar
tips: Make small batches in a clean jar; never top up an old one.
Label the jar with the date you made it.
Whisk in a spoonful of mustard — it holds the emulsion together far better.
Let a cold jar stand a few minutes before shaking; olive oil thickens in the fridge.

faq.q: How long does homemade vinaigrette last?
faq.a: About 2–3 weeks refrigerated at 4 °C or below in a sealed jar. Versions with fresh garlic or shallot are best used sooner.

faq.q: Can you keep homemade vinaigrette out of the fridge?
faq.a: No. Raw garlic, shallot or herbs in oil should be kept cold, not on a shelf. Bring it out for the meal and put it back.
There is no timeline and it does not work — the emulsion splits on thawing and will not shake back together.

faq.q: Why does my vinaigrette go solid in the fridge?
faq.a: Olive oil clouds and thickens in the cold. Stand the jar out for a few minutes and shake hard; it is not spoilage.

zh.name: 自製油醋醬
zh.summary: 自製油醋醬就是油、醋或柑橘汁，加上你想放的東西——芥末、紅蔥、蒜、香草。它屬於冰箱，大約可放 2～3 週。冷凍行不通，因為乳化會分離。
zh.pantry: 檯面不是自製油醋醬該待的地方。酸確實有幫助，但生蒜、紅蔥或新鮮香草懸浮在油裡，是低酸性食材處在缺氧環境，這個組合該冷藏而不是放架上。用餐時拿出來，吃完就放回去——室溫兩小時是原則，廚房超過 32 °C 時縮短為一小時。
zh.fridge: 密封放 4 °C 以下，大約 2～3 週。每次都用乾淨的罐子重做，不要把新的加進舊的裡，並標上製作日期。橄欖油在低溫下會變濁、半凝固，常讓人白緊張一場：拌菜的時候把罐子放著回溫幾分鐘，再用力搖勻就能倒了。含新鮮蒜或紅蔥的版本最好少量製作，並在範圍中較早的那一端用完。
zh.freezer: 自製油醋醬沒有冷凍期限，冷凍也違背了它的意義。解凍後乳化會分離成上層油、下層含水沉澱，怎麼搖都無法真正混回去。一份油醋醬用現有材料兩分鐘就能調好，所以要多少調多少。用不完的話，拿去當醃料或淋在烤蔬菜上更好。
spoilage: 油發出油耗味或蠟筆味
出現氣泡、冒氣或混濁，含蒜的版本尤其要注意
罐內的新鮮香草變黑、變黏
tips: 用乾淨的罐子少量製作；不要把新醬加進舊醬。
加一小匙芥末醬一起打——乳化會穩定很多。
冰過的罐子先放幾分鐘再搖；橄欖油在冰箱裡會變稠。

faq.q: 自製油醋醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封放 4 °C 以下冷藏大約 2～3 週。含新鮮蒜或紅蔥的版本最好更早用完。

faq.q: 自製油醋醬可以不冰嗎？
faq.a: 不行。生蒜、紅蔥或香草泡在油裡應該低溫保存，不要放架上。用餐時拿出來，吃完放回去。
沒有對應期限，而且行不通——解凍後乳化會分離，搖也搖不回來。

faq.q: 油醋醬在冰箱裡凝固了怎麼辦？
faq.a: 橄欖油遇冷會變濁變稠。放著回溫幾分鐘再用力搖勻即可，那不是腐壞。
